itens.titulo: CVE-2026-119977: WordPress WordPress Core Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition Vulnerability
itens.resumo: WordPress WordPress Core contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window. This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades.

itens.titulo: Critical Rails Flaw Lets Attackers Write Server Files via Crafted ImageMagick Uploads
itens.resumo: A critical flaw in Ruby on Rails could allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on an app's server by uploading a crafted file if the app processes uploads using ImageMagick. itens.titulo: Google Issues Patches for Critical Android Flaw That Could Allow RCE Without User Interaction
itens.resumo: A critical Android flaw could allow an attacker to run code on a phone without any user action remotely, Google said in its November security bulletin. itens.titulo: Google Calendar phishing campaign hijacks sessions, bypasses MFA
itens.resumo: A phishing campaign used Google Calendar invites, trusted redirects, and fake login pages to hijack corporate Google sessions and bypass MFA protections. Material Security examines how Operation CloudFire tracked the attacks, blocked malicious messages, and helped take down nearly 900 domains used by the attackers. [...]

itens.titulo: cPGuard Update Channel Hijacked to Backdoor Linux Servers and Collect Password Hashes
itens.resumo: An attacker broke into the update system of the cPGuard security tool on November 2 and used it to send a malicious script to customers' Linux servers. The script installed a backdoor and collected password hashes and other sensitive files from servers that ran it, cPGuard maker OPSSHIELD said in an advisory.
